questions.stem:
George throws a ball at a target 15 times.
Each time George throws the ball, the probability of the ball hitting the target is 0.48

The random variable $X$ represents the number of times George hits the target in 15 throws.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find
(i) $\mathrm{P}(X=3)$
(ii) $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant 5)$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(i) $X\sim \mathrm{B}(15,0.48)$ M1
$\mathrm{P}(X=3)=0.019668\ldots$ awrt 0.0197 A1
(ii) $[\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant 5)=1-\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant 4)]=0.92013\ldots$ awrt 0.920 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
George now throws the ball at the target 250 times.
(b) Use a normal approximation to calculate the probability that he will hit the target more than 110 times.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$Y$ is the number of hits, $M$ is the number of misses. $Y\sim \mathrm{N}(120,62.4)$ or $M\sim \mathrm{N}(130,62.4)$ B1: setting up a correct Normal model.
$\mathrm{P}(X>110)\approx \mathrm{P}(Y>110.5)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z>\dfrac{110.5-120}{\sqrt{62.4}}\right)$ or $\mathrm{P}(X>110)\approx \mathrm{P}(M<139.5)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z<\dfrac{139.5-130}{\sqrt{62.4}}\right)$ M1: sight of the continuity correction with a normal distribution
$=0.88544\ldots$ A1: awrt 0.8854 or awrt 0.885, dependent on sight of $>110.5$ or $<129.5$ or $<139.5$ or $>120.5$

questions.stem:
A manufacturer uses a machine to make metal rods.

The length of a metal rod, $L\,\mathrm{cm}$, is normally distributed with
• a mean of $8\,\mathrm{cm}$
• a standard deviation of $x\,\mathrm{cm}$

Given that the proportion of metal rods less than $7.902\,\mathrm{cm}$ in length is 2.5%

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) show that $x=0.05$ to 2 decimal places.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$[\mathrm{P}(L<7.902)=0.025\Rightarrow]\dfrac{7.902-8}{x}=-1.96$ oe M1
$[x=]0.05$* A1cso
SC B1 (mark as M0A1) for $\dfrac{7.902-8}{0.05}=-1.96\Rightarrow 0.024998$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Calculate the proportion of metal rods that are between $7.94\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $8.09\,\mathrm{cm}$ in length.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: $\mathrm{P}(7.94\leqslant L\leqslant 8.09)=0.8490\ldots$ awrt 0.849 B1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The cost of producing a single metal rod is 20p

A metal rod
• where $L<7.94$ is sold for scrap for 5p
• where $7.94\leqslant L\leqslant 8.09$ is sold for 50p
• where $L>8.09$ is shortened for an extra cost of 10p and then sold for 50p

(c) Calculate the expected profit per 500 of the metal rods.
Give your answer to the nearest pound.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$[\mathrm{P}(L<7.94)=]0.115069\ldots$ (awrt 0.115) or $[\mathrm{P}(L>8.09)=]0.03593\ldots$ (awrt 0.036) B1
$[\mathrm{P}(L<7.94)=]0.115069\ldots$ (awrt 0.115) & $[\mathrm{P}(L>8.09)=]0.03593\ldots$ (awrt 0.036) B1
Expected income per 500 rods $=\sum(\text{Income}\times\text{probability}\times 500)$
$(500\times"0.849"\times0.5)+(500\times"0.1150\ldots"\times0.05)+(500\times"0.03593\ldots"\times0.4)$ or
Expected profit per rod $=\sum(\text{Profit}\times\text{probability})$
$0.30\times"0.849"+-0.15\times"0.1150\ldots"+0.20\times"0.03593\ldots"[=0.2446\ldots]$ M1
Expected profit per 500 rods $500\times\sum(\text{Profit}\times\text{probability})$ or $\sum(\text{Income}\times\text{probability}\times500)-500\times0.2$
$=500\times"0.2446\ldots"$ or $="222.3"-500\times0.2$ M1d
$=[£]122.3\ldots$ awrt [£]122 A1

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The same manufacturer makes metal hinges in large batches.

The hinges each have a probability of 0.015 of having a fault.

A random sample of 200 hinges is taken from each batch and the batch is accepted if fewer than 6 hinges are faulty.

The manufacturer's aim is for 95% of batches to be accepted.

(d) Explain whether the manufacturer is likely to achieve its aim.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Let $X\sim \mathrm{B}(200,0.015)$ M1
$\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant 5)=$ or $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant6)=$ M1
$0.9176\ldots$ or $0.0824$ A1
Manufacturer is unlikely to achieve their aim since $0.9176<0.95$ or Manufacturer is unlikely to achieve their aim since $0.0824>0.05$ A1ft

questions.stem: Dian uses the large data set to investigate the Daily Total Rainfall, $r\,\mathrm{mm}$, for Camborne.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down how a value of $0<r\leqslant 0.05$ is recorded in the large data set.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: tr B1 (Allow Tr or trace or Trace)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Dian uses the data for the 31 days of August 2015 for Camborne and calculates the following statistics
$n=31 \qquad \sum r=174.9 \qquad \sum r^2=3523.283$
(b) Use these statistics to calculate
(i) the mean of the Daily Total Rainfall in Camborne for August 2015,
(ii) the standard deviation of the Daily Total Rainfall in Camborne for August 2015.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(i) $\mu=\dfrac{174.9}{31}=5.6419\ldots$ awrt 5.64 B1
(ii) $\sigma_r=\sqrt{\dfrac{3523.283}{31}-\mu^2}=9.04559\ldots$ awrt 9.05 M1 A1 (For a correct expression for sd including the $\sqrt{}$, ft their mean; A1: awrt 9.05, allow $s=9.1932\ldots$ awrt 9.19; NB awrt to 9.05 or 9.19 with no working is M1A1)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Dian believes that the mean Daily Total Rainfall in August is less in the South of the UK than in the North of the UK.
The mean Daily Total Rainfall in Leuchars for August 2015 is 1.72\,mm to 2 decimal places.
(c) State, giving a reason, whether this provides evidence to support Dian's belief.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
Leuchars is in the North and Camborne is in the South M1 (for stating Leuchars is North of Camborne oe eg Camborne is further south)
The mean is smaller for Leuchars than Camborne therefore there is no evidence that Dian's belief is true A1ft (M1 must be awarded. A correct conclusion and correct comment about the means ft their mean in (b). Allow No.
SC for No and there are only 2 places used so there is insufficient data. Mark as M0A1 on epen)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Dian uses the large data set to estimate the proportion of days with no rain in Camborne for 1987 to be 0.27 to 2 decimal places.
(d) Explain why the distribution B(14, 0.27) might not be a reasonable model for the number of days without rain for a 14-day summer event.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: eg $p=0.27$ is unlikely to be constant. B1 (A correct reason referring to: independence (needs context as to what is independent) eg consecutive 14 days unlikely to be independent; probability [of rain] not being constant; allow a comment that conveys the idea that the proportion of days with no rain will be different over the year.)

questions.stem:
A dentist knows from past records that 10% of customers arrive late for their appointment.

A new manager believes that there has been a change in the proportion of customers who arrive late for their appointment.

A random sample of 50 of the dentist's customers is taken.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write down
• a null hypothesis corresponding to no change in the proportion of customers who arrive late
• an alternative hypothesis corresponding to the manager's belief
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: $\mathrm{H_0}: p=0.1$ $\mathrm{H_1}: p\neq 0.1$ B1 (For both hypotheses in terms of $p$ or $\pi$. Connected to $\mathrm{H_0}$ and $\mathrm{H_1}$ correctly. Condone 10% but not 10)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Using a 5% level of significance, find the critical region for a two-tailed test of the null hypothesis in (a)
You should state the probability of rejection in each tail, which should be less than 0.025
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
Use of $X\sim \mathrm{B}(50,0.1)$ implied by sight of one of awrt 0.0052 or awrt 0.9755 or awrt 0.0245 M1
Critical regions $X=0$ or $X\geqslant 10$ A1
$X=0$ and $X\geqslant 10$ plus $\mathrm{P}(X=0)=$ awrt 0.0052 and $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant10)=$ awrt 0.0245 A1
SC: Both CR correct with no probabilities and no distribution seen scores M0A1A0

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the actual level of significance of the test based on your critical region from part (b)
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: 0.0297 B1ft (awrt 0.0297 or 2.97% or ft for the sum of the probabilities in (b) for "their 2 critical regions" if seen. If none seen it must be awrt 0.0297. SC: M0 in (b) for a one tail test - allow B1ft for their one tail CR in (b) eg 0.0338 or 0.0245 or 0.0579)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The manager observes that 15 of the 50 customers arrived late for their appointment.
(d) With reference to part (b), comment on the manager's belief.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: 15 is in the critical region therefore there is evidence to support the manager's belief B1ft (A correct statement about 15 and "their CR" or sight $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant15)=0.0000738\ldots$ and comparison with "their 0.0245" and a compatible correct statement in context, eg there is evidence that there has been a change in the proportion/probability arriving late. Condone increase rather than change. Do not allow contradicting statements. NB No CR given in (b) then B0)

An employee is chosen at random.

Find the probability that this employee

parts.label: a

(a) is skilled,
(1)

questions.stem:
Anna is investigating the relationship between exercise and resting heart rate.
She takes a random sample of 19 people in her year at school and records for each person
• their resting heart rate, $h$ beats per minute
• the number of minutes, $m$, spent exercising each week

Her results are shown on the scatter diagram.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Interpret the nature of the relationship between $h$ and $m$
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: eg As the number of minutes exercise $(m)$ increases the resting heart rate $(h)$ decreases or the gradient of the curve is becoming flatter with increasing $m$: diminishing effect of each additional minute of exercise B1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Anna codes the data using the formulae
$x=\log_{10} m$
$y=\log_{10} h$
The product moment correlation coefficient between $x$ and $y$ is $-0.897$
(b) Test whether or not there is significant evidence of a negative correlation between $x$ and $y$
You should
• state your hypotheses clearly
• use a 5% level of significance
• state the critical value used
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\mathrm{H_0}: \rho=0$ $\mathrm{H_1}: \rho<0$ B1
Critical value $-0.3887$ (Allow $\pm$) M1
There is evidence that the product moment correlation is less than 0/there is a negative correlation A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The equation of the line of best fit of $y$ on $x$ is
$y=-0.05x+1.92$
(c) Use the equation of the line of best fit of $y$ on $x$ to find a model for $h$ on $m$ in the form
$h=am^k$
where $a$ and $k$ are constants to be found.
(5)
